newsitem.title: USA: Phoenix in default, suspends director, CFO.
newsitem.headline: Phoenix in default, suspends director, CFO.

text.p: Phoenix Shannon Plc said Thursday that it has received informal notices of default under its convertible notes indenture and under its senior loan agreement.
The company said additionally that it has suspended its managing director and chief financial officer and appointed an executive board committee to oversee operations and all on-going matters.
The announcements were made as the company reported that its fiscal 1996 losses would be about $3.5 million, rather than the $200,000 to $300,000 in losses it had projected in July.

The company said it has hired a consulting firm that will report to the board on the company's financial and operating status. It said it will meet with lenders to review covenant compliance issues and discuss short-term and long-term operating plans.
The company said it has deferred payment of $950,000 in interest due November 1 on its 9.50 percent senior subordinated secured convertible notes. There is 30 days' grace for the payment, it said.
